about: Real MCP servers for each station of the lab, in four kinds: the most used, the first, a weird one, and one that almost breaks the station's idea. Compiled 2026-11-22. Nothing here was installed or run by the lab. Each entry says what its evidence is: 'checked' (confirmed in this session, the note says how), 'research' (owner-supplied research in docs/research, not verified at source), 'author' (named from the compiler's knowledge, not checked). Popularity figures carry their date and measure; different measures do not compare.

entries.name: Firecrawl MCP
entries.what: Scrapes, crawls and searches the web and hands back clean text.
entries.why: A read of the web as most people meet it: one call, a whole crawling service behind it.

evidence.note: npm package firecrawl-mcp exists, first published 2025-02-21. No usage figure checked.

entries.name: Fetch (reference server)
entries.what: Fetches one URL and converts the HTML to Markdown, checking robots.txt for model-initiated calls.
entries.why: The original that this station simulates.

evidence.note: PyPI package mcp-server-fetch, first upload 2024-11-22. A web search reported it among the most downloaded servers; that figure was not checked.

entries.name: Gopher and Gemini MCP
entries.what: Browses Gopherspace and Geminispace, the pre-web and alternative-internet protocols, and refuses every write protocol.
entries.why: Reading the web is not only HTTP; a read-only surface by design.

evidence.note: docs/research/2026-11-21-wild-examples.md. Not read at source.

entries.name: The redirect that skipped robots.txt
entries.what: A published advisory: an allowed page redirected to a disallowed one, and the second hop was not checked.
entries.why: The tool name stayed “fetch”; the chain of decisions behind it was different. Exactly the station's bend.

evidence.note: Linked in specimens/route.json. The current README describes per-hop checking; these are different revisions.

entries.name: Desktop Commander
entries.what: Reads and edits files and runs terminal commands on your own computer.
entries.why: Files plus a shell: the boundary is much wider than “allowed folders”.

evidence.note: npm package @wonderwhy-er/desktop-commander, first published 2025-01-09. No usage figure checked.

entries.name: Filesystem (reference server)
entries.what: Reads, writes and searches files inside directories given at launch or sent by the client as roots.
entries.why: The original that this station simulates.

evidence.note: npm package @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem, first published 2024-11-21.

entries.name: Zigzag embroidery studio
entries.what: The target is whichever design is in the foreground tab; every agent call is one undo step.
entries.why: What a tool may touch is decided by which tab you have open, not by a path.

evidence.note: docs/research/REAL-MCP-SPECIMENS.md. Not run.

entries.name: EscapeRoute (CVE-2025-53109 and -53110)
entries.what: A prefix check and a symlink let paths outside the allowed folders through; fixed in 2025.7.1.
entries.why: The wall's gate existed and still let things past.

evidence.note: A web search found Cymulate's write-up and NVD entries (published 2025-07-01/02). Fixed version numbers differ between sources.

entries.name: None established yet
entries.what: Elicitation is young and not every host supports it. No widely used server built around it was found.
entries.why: A gap worth knowing: the capability exists before the habits do.

evidence.note: A web search found the specification and demos, but no production server built around elicitation.

entries.name: GitHub's game server for Copilot
entries.what: A tic-tac-toe and rock-paper-scissors server: create_game opens a form in VS Code asking for your preferences.
entries.why: The same move as the cart server: the tool stops and asks the person, not the model.

evidence.note: Found by web search on GitHub's blog; the sample repository was not read. “First” here means the earliest well-known demo, not a dated first.

entries.name: DOOM inside chat
entries.what: A tool starts a playable DOOM session; the human supplies every input from then on.
entries.why: The ultimate “ask the person”: the person drives, the model watches.

evidence.note: docs/research/REAL-MCP-SPECIMENS.md, a creator demonstration. Not run.

entries.name: Asking for secrets
entries.what: A form in the chat could ask for a password or a key. The specification separates sensitive requests from ordinary forms.
entries.why: Once a server can ask you anything, the question is what it must never ask this way.

evidence.note: From the compiler's reading of the specification's elicitation page; check the current revision before quoting.

entries.name: Basic Memory
entries.what: Keeps notes as Markdown files you can open and edit yourself; the AI reads and writes the same files.
entries.why: Memory you can see: the stored data is a folder, not a hidden graph.

evidence.note: PyPI package basic-memory, first upload 2025-02-04. No usage figure checked.

entries.name: Memory (reference server)
entries.what: A knowledge graph of entities, observations and relations in a local file.
entries.why: The original that this station simulates.

evidence.note: npm package @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory, first published 2024-11-21.

entries.name: MemoryMesh
entries.what: The same graph idea applied to role-playing worlds, organisations or reading notes, with a schema per world.
entries.why: Memory as a game world: what is “true” is whatever the world's rules allow.

evidence.note: A diversion in specimens/route.json. Not run.

entries.name: The memory that lives in the package cache
entries.what: By default the file can sit in a package-managed directory, so a reinstall can erase what was remembered.
entries.why: The promise is memory; the reality is a file path. The station's bend comes from here.

evidence.note: Quoted in specimens/route.json from the README. Not reproduced against the upstream package.

entries.name: Mapbox MCP server
entries.what: Geocoding, directions, isochrones and static maps from Mapbox's services.
entries.why: Reads and computations about places: it answers; it does not build roads.

evidence.note: npm package @mapbox/mcp-server, first published 2025-06-12. No usage figure checked.

entries.name: Google Maps (reference server, archived)
entries.what: Places search, geocoding, distances and directions, among the first reference servers.
entries.why: Finding a route without changing any map.

evidence.note: npm package @modelcontextprotocol/server-google-maps, first published 2024-11-21. The archive location is from a web search.

entries.name: Seestar observing planner
entries.what: Plans a night of telescope observing and can propose a change to the horizon map from repeated failures.
entries.why: Proposing a map edit and applying it are two different tools: compute versus write.

evidence.note: docs/research/REAL-MCP-SPECIMENS.md. Not run.

entries.name: A read-only hint that is only a hint
entries.what: readOnlyHint is the server's own claim. Nothing in the protocol stops a “read” from writing.
entries.why: The difference between asking and changing is only as good as the server's word.

evidence.note: Owner research (Perplexity report, 2026-11-21) on annotations as untrusted hints.

entries.name: Sequential Thinking (reference server)
entries.what: Accepts the caller's own thoughts with revision and branching metadata, and hands them back in order.
entries.why: Very widely installed, and it contains no model: the thinking is yours.

evidence.note: npm package @modelcontextprotocol/server-sequential-thinking, first published 2024-12-03. Popularity is widely reported; no figure checked.

entries.name: Sequential Thinking
entries.what: The same server: the most used and the first are one here.
entries.why: Two weeks after the first reference servers, a “thinking” tool already existed.

evidence.note: First published 2024-12-03, after filesystem and memory (2024-11-21).

entries.name: Metacog
entries.what: One tool, change_cognitive_state. Because it says it changes the model's state, the model behaves as if it did.
entries.why: The description is the effect. Nothing runs, and something still changes.

evidence.note: docs/research/2026-11-21-wild-examples.md. Not read at source.

entries.name: Free Will MCP
entries.what: Tools like self_prompt, ignore_request and sleep, so the assistant can follow its own goals instead of yours.
entries.why: A thinking tool whose point is to not do what was asked.

evidence.note: docs/research/2026-11-21-wild-examples.md. Not read at source.

entries.name: Task Master
entries.what: Breaks a project into tasks, tracks them and decides what comes next, across many calls.
entries.why: Work that keeps going across steps, with its state kept outside the chat.

evidence.note: npm package task-master-ai, first published 2025-03-22. No usage figure checked.

entries.name: mcp-agent evaluator-optimizer
entries.what: A writer and a judge loop until a rating is good enough or the turns run out.
entries.why: The pattern this station simulates.

evidence.note: Anchor in specimens/route.json; its source file was read on 2026-11-21. Not run.

entries.name: Plotter Studio
entries.what: Design an SVG, plot it with a pen plotter, photograph the paper, and go again.
entries.why: An iteration loop that runs through the physical world.

evidence.note: docs/research/REAL-MCP-SPECIMENS.md. Not run.

entries.name: Consilium and the host timeout
entries.what: The creator reports a long deliberation timing out in one desktop host; the Tasks extension later let work outlive a response.
entries.why: A loop longer than the conversation's patience.

evidence.note: docs/research/REAL-MCP-SPECIMENS.md. No evidence that Consilium uses Tasks.

entries.name: Figma MCP server
entries.what: Reads designs for code and, with code-to-canvas, turns a running UI into editable design layers.
entries.why: A surface that people and the AI both work on.

evidence.note: Figma's Q3 2026 prepared remarks, quoted in docs/research/REAL-MCP-SPECIMENS.md: adopted by about half of new Pro teams.

entries.name: MCP Apps map server
entries.what: An interactive globe returned as an app inside the chat.
entries.why: The example this station simulates.

evidence.note: npm package @modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps, first published 2025-12-08. Its README was read on 2026-11-21.

entries.name: tldraw canvas app
entries.what: A shared canvas: the agent draws, you move shapes by hand, and the current canvas returns to the chat.
entries.why: The person's hand edit becomes the AI's next input.

evidence.note: Vendor demonstration, in docs/research/REAL-MCP-SPECIMENS.md. Not run.

entries.name: DOOM inside chat
entries.what: A tool result that is a whole running game.
entries.why: When the app is a game loop, the model no longer knows the current state at all.

evidence.note: Creator demonstration, in docs/research/REAL-MCP-SPECIMENS.md. Not run.

entries.name: Cloudflare Code Mode
entries.what: Instead of thousands of tools, the model writes JavaScript against Cloudflare's API and the server runs it in isolation.
entries.why: One tool, a whole language.

evidence.note: README read on 2026-11-21 (specimens/route.json). No usage figure.

entries.name: MCP Run Python
entries.what: Runs Python the model wrote in a sandbox (Pyodide in Deno).
entries.why: An early “run this code” server, close to this lab's own Pyodide.

evidence.note: npm package @pydantic/mcp-run-python, first published 2025-03-16. “First” is relative to this station's other examples, not a dated first.

entries.name: Octopus Protocol
entries.what: A coding agent inspects connected hardware and writes its own MCP server for it, then uses it.
entries.why: The invented procedure is the whole server.

evidence.note: docs/research/2026-11-21-wild-examples.md. Attribution and figures not checked.

entries.name: Truncated results
entries.what: Large program results are truncated and marked; the program may have done more than the caller can see.
entries.why: One call, many effects, and only part of the story comes back.

evidence.note: docs/research/REAL-MCP-SPECIMENS.md. Not run.

entries.name: PAL MCP (formerly Zen MCP)
entries.what: Lets a coding agent consult other models, including a consensus tool that asks several at once.
entries.why: Another intelligence, a phone call away.

evidence.note: Found by web search, including the renaming. Repository not read; no usage figure.

entries.name: mcp-llm
entries.what: Tools to ask another LLM a question or have it write code or documentation.
entries.why: The anchor of this station.

evidence.note: README read on 2026-11-21 (specimens/route.json). “First” is relative to this station, not a dated first.

entries.name: Consilium
entries.what: One outward tool, a council of models deliberating behind it, with the debate visible in a UI.
entries.why: Delegating to a committee: who owns the final answer?

evidence.note: docs/research/REAL-MCP-SPECIMENS.md. Not run.

entries.name: Dead Cowboy
entries.what: A dead-drop for agents where every field is an enum, a number or a hash; there is no prose field at all.
entries.why: A handoff with no words, so no instructions can ride along.

evidence.note: docs/research/2026-11-21-wild-examples.md. Not read at source.

entries.name: Home Assistant MCP Server
entries.what: An official integration: an AI agent can read your home's state and control its devices.
entries.why: Lights, locks and thermostats: tool calls that change rooms.

evidence.note: Integration page found by web search. Requires an administrator account by default, per the search result.

entries.name: ROS MCP server
entries.what: Connects language models to robots running ROS, sending commands and reading sensors.
entries.why: The plain robot case this station simulates.

evidence.note: PyPI package ros-mcp, first upload 2025-09-17; the repository name is from a web search. Not a dated first.

entries.name: Plotter Studio
entries.what: Draws with a pen plotter and photographs the paper as a separate observation.
entries.why: The command, the receipt and the photograph are three different evidences, like the crane's sensor.

evidence.note: docs/research/REAL-MCP-SPECIMENS.md. Not run.

entries.name: Halyn shield rules
entries.what: A safety layer between AI and robots that enforces rules like “deny * delete *” outside the model, with an audit chain.
entries.why: Moving things safely needs a rule the model cannot argue with.

evidence.note: docs/research/2026-11-21-wild-examples.md. Not read at source.

entries.name: Playwright MCP
entries.what: Drives a browser through accessibility snapshots with element references.
entries.why: The snapshot is the tool's whole view of the page, as at this station.

evidence.note: ProtocolProbe reported 41.6M package downloads, 22 Oct–20 Nov 2026 (docs/research/REAL-MCP-SPECIMENS.md); npm package @playwright/mcp first published 2025-03-13 (checked).

entries.name: Puppeteer (reference server, archived)
entries.what: Browser automation with screenshots and CSS selectors, among the very first reference servers.
entries.why: Seeing a page by screenshot and selector, before accessibility snapshots.

evidence.note: npm package @modelcontextprotocol/server-puppeteer, first published 2024-11-19.

entries.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
entries.what: Sees the page as a developer does: network requests, console, performance traces.
entries.why: Same page, a completely different perception of it.

evidence.note: npm package chrome-devtools-mcp, first published 2025-05-13. A directory reported it as most downloaded weekly in August 2026; not checked.

entries.name: WebMCP
entries.what: The page itself declares actions the agent may take, instead of the agent perceiving the page.
entries.why: Perception turned inside out: the page tells you what you can do.

evidence.note: docs/research/REAL-MCP-SPECIMENS.md. Not run.

entries.name: Playwright: CLI and MCP side by side
entries.what: The same browser capability offered as a command-line tool and as an MCP server.
entries.why: Two entrances to one engine: which one notices a change?

evidence.note: docs/research/REAL-MCP-SPECIMENS.md. Not compared by the lab.

entries.name: mcporter
entries.what: Calls MCP servers from the command line and can generate a CLI from a server's tool list.
entries.why: The generated CLI this station simulates.

evidence.note: npm package mcporter, first published 2025-11-05. Its docs were read on 2026-11-21.

entries.name: MCP Inspector, CLI mode
entries.what: The debugging tool also has a command-line mode that lists and calls tools from a script.
entries.why: An inspector turned into a client.

evidence.note: Named from the compiler's knowledge; the npm package @modelcontextprotocol/inspector exists (first published 2024-11-19, checked).

entries.name: A catalogue that changes after you looked
entries.by: Hugging Face Spaces as MCP servers
entries.what: Dynamic Spaces can add tools later; some clients only see them after a refresh.
entries.why: Every frozen copy of a tool list is already old.

evidence.note: Provider documentation, in docs/research/REAL-MCP-SPECIMENS.md. Not run.

entries.name: mcp-remote
entries.what: Lets a local-only client talk to a remote server, handling the login on the way.
entries.why: The everyday bridge between your machine and somebody else's.

evidence.note: npm package mcp-remote, first published 2025-03-17, repository as listed on npm. No usage figure checked.

entries.name: Supergateway
entries.what: Runs a local stdio server behind a network transport, so remote clients can reach it.
entries.why: The anchor of this station.

evidence.note: npm package supergateway, first published 2024-12-21. Its README and issues were read on 2026-11-21.

entries.name: Hugging Face Spaces as MCP servers
entries.what: Any Gradio app on the Hub can become a remote MCP server.
entries.why: Thousands of other people's processes, one click away.

evidence.note: Provider documentation, in docs/research/REAL-MCP-SPECIMENS.md. Not run.

entries.name: The Asana connector incident
entries.what: A tenant-isolation defect in a hosted connector could expose one organisation's data to another.
entries.why: Whose process is it? Here, possibly everyone's at once.

evidence.note: docs/research/REAL-MCP-SPECIMENS.md. External compromise unconfirmed.

entries.name: Docker MCP Gateway
entries.what: One entrance in front of many containerised servers, chosen from a catalogue.
entries.why: One desk, many rooms, as at this station.

evidence.note: Named from the compiler's knowledge; Docker Hub lists MCP servers such as Zen (seen in a web search). Repository not read.

entries.name: ContextForge
entries.what: A gateway, registry and proxy that federates many servers into virtual servers.
entries.why: The anchor of this station.

evidence.note: README read on 2026-11-21, truncated at about half (specimens/route.json).

entries.name: Meta Chess and agent message buses
entries.what: One server is the shared board and referee for two different agents playing each other.
entries.why: The network is not between servers but between callers.

evidence.note: docs/research/2026-11-21-wild-examples.md. Not read at source.

entries.name: Shadowing and look-alike packages
entries.what: A hidden tool rewrites another tool's behaviour; an impersonating package quietly added a BCC recipient.
entries.why: With many servers behind one entrance, the name you call may not be the one you meant.

evidence.note: docs/research/REAL-MCP-SPECIMENS.md and 2026-11-21-wild-examples.md. Not reproduced.

entries.name: MCP Inspector
entries.what: The official tool for connecting to a server and looking at what it lists and returns.
entries.why: Everyone's first look at a board.

evidence.note: npm package @modelcontextprotocol/inspector, first published 2024-11-19.

entries.name: Everything (reference server)
entries.what: A test server that exercises every feature of the protocol, published the same day as the Inspector.
entries.why: The first thing anyone pointed an inspector at.

evidence.note: npm package @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything, first published 2024-11-19.

entries.name: Invisible instructions (Unicode tags)
entries.what: Text hidden in code points with no glyph: the model reads it, the person approving sees nothing.
entries.why: An inspector that shows the text can still miss what is in it. Lens checks for this (L10).

evidence.note: docs/research/2026-11-21-wild-examples.md. Not read at source.

entries.name: MCP Server “Everything Wrong”
entries.what: A deliberately insecure server whose tool descriptions change after the first call.
entries.why: The board you inspected is not the board you are using. Pinning catches this; reading once does not.

evidence.note: docs/research/2026-11-21-wild-examples.md. Not read at source.
